text_blocks.snippet: Raynaud's phenomenon, also known as Raynaud's disease or Raynaud's syndrome, is a condition that affects blood vessels, primarily in the fingers and toes. It causes the blood vessels to narrow (vasospasm) in response to cold or stress, leading to reduced blood flow and characteristic color changes and numbness.
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition that affects blood vessels, primarily in the fingers and toes

list.title: Episodic attacks:
list.snippet: Symptoms occur in episodes, triggered by cold exposure or emotional stress.

list.title: Color changes:
list.snippet: Affected areas, typically fingers and toes, may turn white (pallor), then blue (cyanosis), and finally red (rubor) as blood flow returns.

list.title: Numbness and pain:
list.snippet: Reduced blood flow can cause numbness, tingling, and pain in the affected areas.

list.title: Skin ulcers and gangrene (in severe cases):
list.snippet: Prolonged episodes of vasospasm can lead to painful sores and, in rare cases, tissue damage.
